title: Systems Synergy
hook: Having a lot of systems isn't the same as having systems that actually help each other.
statement: Line up your systems so one action feeds more than one goal. That's where the compounding comes from.
explainer: Two good routines that never touch just add up. Two that are built to overlap give you more than the sum. That only happens if you design it on purpose.
sop: Map your main areas, like health, business, relationships, and learning.
Spot one action that could serve two of them at once.
Check whether your systems are aligned or quietly fighting each other.
Redesign one routine to do double duty, like a walking client call.
Track whether the combo actually beats doing them separately.
equation_example: System A makes 5, System B makes 5. Run apart, the sum is 10. Aligned, the Total hits 13. Misaligned, they get in each other's way and you get 7. Above the sum means real synergy. At or below means they're just coexisting.
question: Pick two things you do every week and write down one way to merge them into a single action.
closing_statement: Two aligned systems can outdo three separate ones.
caption:
Principle Nº 229: Systems Synergy

Having a lot of systems isn't the same as having systems that actually help each other.

Line up your systems so one action feeds more than one goal. That's where the compounding comes from.

Your turn: Pick two things you do every week and write down one way to merge them into a single action.
